At the time when I am developing HAPPI agent, of course the most important aspect of any AI agent are the tools. HAPPI agent should obviously be able to read any class data, graph (history) data, commit class data and so on. and because I started to work on this huge codebase as frontend developer, the first thing that comes to my mind is that all those read and write functions are already laid down on our websocket API like FetchClassData, FetchGraphDataEx, CommitClassData and so on. So I proceed right away by developing the tool for the AI agent, and the first tool that I implement is the fetch_class_data tool. When devloping this tool, I found myself, copying the logic in #sym:FetchClassData to the HAPPI agent fetch_class_data tool definition. So that got me thinking that parts of this should then be extracted out so that it can be shared by both cMiaServer and HAPPI agent tool definition. So I did implement that in this branch. this is the main focus on this branch, extracting those parts of websocket API that can be reused by HAPPI agent tool definition.

but then I got strong rejection from our architects about this approach. He just could not see why this DataOperations library really needed. I give him this image to try to convince himbut he still questioned it. Even after I presented to him that I want and already have using it in HAPPI-draft branch. then he ask me back "why don't you just use VtrinLib directly?" why dont the agent just use GetInstancesWithSecurityChecking that is available in VtrinLib. That got me thinking. The only reason why I am thinking of modelling the tool based on the existing websocket API was just because that is what i am more familiar with for read write operation to RTDB. but for backend devlopers, the go to API is indeed usually VtrinLib. Although VtrinLib is more of an SDK. But All in all, this really got me thinking hard. Does it mean that my approach of providing this fetch_class_data tool to happi agent is non optimal in the first place and not good approach architecturally. Should I entirely abandon this branch and should I totally revamp this branch. Should I really re-think set of tools to give to HAPPI agent, should it really be modeled after the existing websocket API?

what do you think?

So I proceed right away by developing the tool for the AI agent. And the first tool that I implement is the fetch class data tool. The AI Docs API system architecture in that branch explains what HAPPI stands for—History Agent Platform for Process Intelligence. At the time I was developing the HAPPI agent, the most important aspect of any AI agent, of course, is the tools. HAPPI agents should be able to read any class data, access graph history data, commit class data, and so on.

Since I started working on this large codebase as a front-end developer, my first thought was that all those read and write functions were already implemented in our WebSocket API—like FetchClassData, FetchGraphDataEx, CommitClassData, and others. So I proceeded to develop the tool for the AI agent, and the first tool I implemented was fetch_class_data. While developing this tool, I found myself copying logic from FetchClassData into the HAPPI agent's fetch_class_data tool definition. That made me think: should parts of this be extracted out so they can be shared by both cMiaServer and the HAPPI agent tool definition? I implemented this in the branch, making the main focus extracting and reusing those parts of the WebSocket API in the HAPPI agent tool definition.

However, I received strong rejection from our architect regarding this approach. He could not see why the DataOperations library was needed. I even showed him an image to explain, but he still questioned it. Even after demonstrating that I wanted and was already using it in the HAPPI-draft branch, he asked, "Why don’t you just use VtrinLib directly? Why doesn’t the agent just use GetInstancesWithSecurityChecking, which is available in VtrinLib?" That really got me thinking. The only reason I modeled the tool based on the WebSocket API was because I'm more familiar with using it for read/write operations to RTDB. For backend developers, however, the go-to API is usually VtrinLib, although VtrinLib is more of an SDK. 

All of this really made me consider whether my approach—providing the fetch_class_data tool to the HAPPI agent modeled after the WebSocket API—is non-optimal from an architectural standpoint. Should I completely abandon this branch? Should I refactor it entirely? Should I rethink the set of tools provided to the HAPPI agent? Should it be modeled after the existing WebSocket API, or is that the wrong direction?
